name: LCR Meter
summary: Instrument that measures inductance, capacitance and resistance, plus quality factor and dissipation factor.
overview: An LCR meter measures the impedance of a component by applying a small AC test signal at a chosen frequency and measuring the voltage and current. From this it calculates inductance (L), capacitance (C) and resistance (R), along with D (dissipation factor), Q (quality factor), ESR and phase angle. A handheld meter has an LCD, a few keys and a test socket or test leads. Components must be removed from live circuits and capacitors discharged before measuring. Based on DER EE DE-5000.

parts.name: LCD Display
parts.function: Shows the primary reading (L, C, R or Z) and a secondary reading (D, Q, ESR or phase angle), together with the unit, test frequency, series or parallel mode and status symbols.
parts.usage: Read the value together with the unit prefix (for example nF or mH) and the symbols for the equivalent circuit and frequency. A very large or unstable value can mean the component is not connected.
safety: A low-battery symbol means readings may be wrong; replace the battery before relying on measurements.

parts.name: Power Button
parts.function: Switches the meter on and off.
parts.usage: Press to switch on and, usually, to switch off. Most meters also turn off automatically after a period without key presses.
safety: Switch the meter off before opening the battery cover.

parts.name: LCR / Auto Button
parts.function: Selects the measured quantity: automatic recognition of L, C or R, or a fixed inductance, capacitance or resistance mode.
parts.usage: Press to cycle through the modes. Auto mode picks the likely quantity but can be wrong for unusual parts, so choose the mode manually if the result looks odd.
safety: Check the mode symbol on the display before you record a reading.

parts.name: DCR Button
parts.function: Measures the DC resistance of the component, as opposed to its AC impedance. It is useful for inductor windings.
parts.usage: Press DCR, connect an inductor or resistor and read the resistance. Compare to the datasheet DC resistance value.
safety: Use DCR only on components that are not connected to a power source.

parts.name: FREQ Button
parts.function: Changes the test frequency, for example between 100 Hz, 120 Hz, 1 kHz, 10 kHz and 100 kHz, depending on the model.
parts.usage: Press FREQ to step through the available frequencies. Use a frequency close to the one the component operates at, as capacitance and inductance values vary with frequency.
safety: Do not compare readings taken at different frequencies without noting the frequency used.

parts.name: SER / PAR Button
parts.function: Selects the series or parallel equivalent circuit model used to calculate the displayed value.
parts.usage: Use the series model for low-impedance parts such as large capacitors and small inductors, and the parallel model for high-impedance parts such as small capacitors and large inductors, or use the automatic setting.
safety: Record which model was used when writing down a measurement.

parts.name: HOLD Button
parts.function: Freezes the displayed reading so it can be read after the component is removed.
parts.usage: Press HOLD to freeze the display and press again to release. The HOLD symbol shows while it is active.
safety: Release HOLD before the next measurement; a frozen reading does not update.

parts.name: Test Socket
parts.function: Input connection for the test fixture or leads. Components are placed in the fixture or clipped to the leads so the meter can drive and measure them.
parts.usage: Plug in the fixture or leads firmly before switching on. Insert the component leads into the fixture, or clip the leads across the component.
safety: Never apply an external voltage to the test socket.
Discharge capacitors fully before connecting them to the meter.

parts.name: Test Leads / Clips
parts.function: Lead set with clips or tweezers for measuring components that do not fit the socket or fixture, including surface-mount parts.
parts.usage: Short the clips together and use the meter's zero or open/short calibration function if it has one, then clip across the component. Keep the leads short and still during a measurement.
safety: Do not clip the leads on a live circuit.
Replace leads that have cracked insulation or loose clips.

parts.name: Battery Cover
parts.function: Covers the compartment that holds the battery which powers the meter. Some models can also run from a DC adapter.
parts.usage: Open the cover with the meter off and the leads removed, replace the battery with the correct type and polarity, and close the cover.
safety: Remove the leads and switch off before opening the battery compartment.
Do not leave flat batteries in the meter for long; they can leak.

safetyRules: Measure components only when they are removed from the circuit and the circuit is powered off.
Discharge every capacitor, especially large electrolytic and high-voltage types, before connecting it to the meter. A charged capacitor can damage the meter and give you a shock.
Never apply external voltage to the meter's test terminals.
Do not touch the component leads with your fingers while measuring small values, since body capacitance disturbs the reading.
Check the battery state and inspect the leads for damage before use.

steps.text: Make sure the capacitor is out of the circuit and fully discharged.
Plug the test fixture or leads into the meter.
Switch the meter on with the power button.
Press LCR until the capacitance mode (C) is selected, or use auto mode.
Press FREQ to select a test frequency suited to the capacitor, for example 1 kHz for most values.
Choose the series or parallel model with the SER/PAR button if required.
Insert the capacitor into the fixture or clip the leads across it, observing polarity for electrolytic types.
Read the capacitance and the D or ESR value on the display and compare it to the marked value and tolerance.
Press HOLD if you need to freeze the value, then switch the meter off.

procedures.title: Measure inductance and winding resistance of an inductor

steps.text: Remove the inductor from the circuit and make sure no power is connected.
Press LCR to select inductance mode (L).
Set the test frequency with FREQ, using a frequency near the inductor's use.
Clip the leads across the inductor, away from large metal objects.
Read the inductance and Q value on the display.
Press DCR to measure the winding's DC resistance.
Compare the readings with the datasheet values, and switch the meter off.

faults.symptom: A 10 pF capacitor reads 14 pF and the value drifts when you move your hand near the leads.

options.text: Stray and body capacitance from long leads and nearby objects

faults.explanation: At picofarad values, lead and body capacitance are significant. Keep the leads short, use the fixture, keep your hands away and do an open/short calibration if the meter offers it.

faults.symptom: A power inductor measures 30 percent lower than its marking at 100 kHz, but is close to the marked value at 1 kHz.

options.text: Inductance depends on test frequency and the part is specified at a different frequency
The inductor must be burnt out

faults.explanation: The effective inductance of a real inductor changes with frequency because of core and winding effects. Measure at the frequency given in the datasheet before judging the part.

faults.symptom: After a large electrolytic capacitor was connected straight from a power supply board, the meter shows nothing and no longer measures capacitance.

options.text: The capacitor was still charged and has damaged the meter's input
The test frequency was too low
The DCR key was pressed first

faults.explanation: The meter input is not designed to withstand external voltage. A charged capacitor can destroy the input circuit. Always discharge capacitors through a suitable resistor before connecting them.

questions.prompt: What does an LCR meter measure?
questions.explanation: L is inductance, C is capacitance and R is resistance.

questions.prompt: What must you do to a capacitor before connecting it to the meter?
questions.explanation: A charged capacitor can damage the meter and give a shock hazard. Discharge it first.

questions.prompt: Can an LCR meter be used on a powered circuit?
options: No, components must be unpowered and out of circuit
questions.explanation: The meter supplies its own test signal. External voltage or parallel parts give wrong readings or damage it.

questions.prompt: What does the D (dissipation factor) value indicate?
options: The ratio of energy lost to energy stored, i.e. how lossy the component is
questions.explanation: D is the ratio of the resistive to the reactive part of the impedance. Lower D means a better, lower-loss component.

questions.prompt: Q (quality factor) is the reciprocal of which value?
questions.explanation: Q = 1/D. It is usually quoted for inductors, while D is usually quoted for capacitors.

options: Component values and losses change with frequency
questions.explanation: Capacitors and inductors are specified at particular frequencies and real values vary with frequency.

questions.prompt: Which equivalent model is normally better for a small, high-impedance capacitor?
options: Either gives the same result at all values
questions.explanation: High-impedance parts are better described by the parallel model; low-impedance parts by the series model.

questions.prompt: Why should your fingers not touch the leads when measuring a few picofarads?
options: Body capacitance adds to the reading
questions.explanation: Your body and nearby objects add stray capacitance that matters for very small values.

questions.prompt: What is the DCR function used for?
options: Measuring a component's DC resistance, such as an inductor winding
questions.explanation: DCR measures the DC resistance of a winding or resistor, which is separate from its AC impedance.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the open/short calibration, where the meter offers it?
options: To remove the effect of lead and fixture stray impedance
questions.explanation: Calibrating with the leads open and then shorted compensates for the fixture and lead errors, improving accuracy for small values.
